- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) and forecast is flat or rising slowly, model tends to underpredict sharp spikes; correct by adding 2–5% to forecast if sentiment > 0.7.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3) and forecast is rising, model often overestimates; reduce forecast by 3–8% if sentiment < -0.2.
- After a large spike in price (true > 85), model frequently overcorrects and underpredicts the next peak; add 1–3% to forecast for 2–3 days post-spike.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.3) and forecast is trending, model often fails to capture mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with 30-day moving average if sentiment swings > 0.2.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates true outcomes when sentiment is > 0.6; apply a +3% bias to forecast if sentiment > 0.65.
- If sentiment is low (≤ 0.3) and forecast is rising, model often overestimates; reduce forecast by 5–10% if sentiment < 0.2.
- Model tends to lag in predicting true outcomes when sentiment is high and price is volatile; add 1–2 days of lag correction (i.e., shift forecast 1–2 days ahead) if sentiment > 0.7 and volatility > 0.1.
